record.title: EmbodiedRSI reports hypothesis-guided harness evolution with transfer to five real-robot tasks
record.summary: Song et al. introduce EmbodiedRSI, a harness around a frozen robot foundation model that selects physical experiments by value of information, co-evolves code and skills, and learns which memories improve later adaptation. The 7 October 2026 preprint reports 77.0% overall success on RoboCasa365 and 71.3% on Composite-Unseen versus 40.1% for Harness VLA; on LIBERO-Pro it reports 86.8% versus 72.1%. On a physical SO-101 arm, the authors report 71.3% success across five tasks versus 46.0% for SmolVLA alone, with 30 trials per condition per task. These are author-reported results, not independently reproduced. The physical evaluation is limited to five tasks; the harness lowers success on the glasses-grasp task, and the foundation model is not updated.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Song et al. introduce a harness that selects robot experiments using a hypothesis graph and value-of-information score, co-evolves executable code and skills, and trains memory actions from downstream reward while keeping the robot foundation model frozen during trials.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On RoboCasa365, the authors report 77.0% overall success and 71.3% on Composite-Unseen, versus 40.1% for Harness VLA on Composite-Unseen; on LIBERO-Pro they report 86.8% versus 72.1% for Harness VLA.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On a physical SO-101 arm, the authors report that EmbodiedRSI's simulation-evolved harness raises success from 46.0% to 71.3% overall across five tasks, with 30 trials per condition per task; success falls on Glasses Bridge Grasp from 60.0% to 56.7%.

claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.text: The reported results establish broad recursive self-improvement of robot foundation models.

contradictory_evidence: In the physical task table, glasses-bridge-grasp success falls from 60.0% with SmolVLA alone to 56.7% with the EmbodiedRSI harness, despite an aggregate gain across five tasks.
The paper's zero-shot sim-to-real framing refers to transferring the harness; the backbone was fine-tuned using 50 teleoperated demonstrations for each task before physical testing.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the simulation or five-task physical results was conducted, and a public implementation/data release was not established.
Physical evidence is limited to one SO-101 arm, one fine-tuned SmolVLA backbone and five tasks; transfer across robots, backbones, labs and task distributions is unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported results generalize, selecting informative robot trials and retaining reusable code-skill improvements could materially reduce physical-data needs for robot adaptation. A 6 reflects a major research-engineering advance with reported physical trials, while one paper, one arm and five tasks leave transfer and reproducibility uncertain.
limitations: All performance numbers are author-reported; the research desk did not independently execute code or reproduce simulation or physical trials.
The physical evaluation uses one SO-101 arm, one SmolVLA backbone and five selected tasks. Its pooled 71.3% gain is not a general robot-transfer rate.
The harness reduces success on Glasses Bridge Grasp from 60.0% to 56.7%; outcomes are not uniformly improved.

The underlying robot model is fine-tuned on 50 teleoperated demonstrations per physical task for 20,000 steps using four H200 GPUs before trials; only the harness transfers zero-shot and the backbone remains frozen during trials.
The paper reports simulation seeds and trial counts but does not establish independent replication, broad hardware transfer or deployment cost per successful task.
The model parameters are not updated; the evidence concerns harness-level adaptation, not recursive self-improvement of the foundation model.
brief.summary: Song et al. introduce EmbodiedRSI, a harness around a frozen robot foundation model that selects physical experiments by value of information, co-evolves code and skills, and learns which memories improve later adaptation. The 7 October 2026 preprint reports 77.0% overall success on RoboCasa365 and 71.3% on Composite-Unseen versus 40.1% for Harness VLA; on LIBERO-Pro it reports 86.8% versus 72.1%. On a physical SO-101 arm, the authors report 71.3% success across five tasks versus 46.0% for SmolVLA alone, with 30 trials per condition per task. These are author-reported results, not independently reproduced. The physical evaluation is limited to five tasks; the harness lowers success on the glasses-grasp task, and the foundation model is not updated.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report RoboCasa365 success of 77.0% overall and 71.3% on Composite-Unseen versus 40.1% for Harness VLA; LIBERO-Pro success of 86.8% versus 72.1%; and SO-101 physical-task success of 71.3% versus 46.0% for SmolVLA alone. The physical result pools five tasks with 30 trials per condition per task.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv v1 establishes that the authors published this method and reported the stated tables and setup. the research desk did not execute the code or reproduce the results.
technical.implementation_status: The paper and project page were inspected. No public implementation repository or independently usable artifacts were established in this review.
technical.mechanism: A Fast System maintains competing code and skill hypotheses, selects matched physical experiments by expected information gain per estimated cost, and uses outcomes to revise code and skills jointly. A Slow System builds hierarchical memory and trains a policy to select memory actions based on downstream task improvement, uncertainty reduction and experiment cost. The robot foundation model remains frozen during execution; the paper's real-robot setup fine-tunes SmolVLA before trials.
technical.regime: One arXiv v1 paper; RoboCasa365 and LIBERO-Pro simulations plus an SO-101 physical arm, SmolVLA backbone, five physical tasks, 30 trials per condition per task. Before physical evaluation, the authors collect 50 teleoperated demonstrations per task and fine-tune SmolVLA for 20,000 steps on four NVIDIA H200 GPUs; SmolVLA is then frozen during trials.
technical.reproducibility: Reported simulation uses ten random seeds and ten evaluation trials per task, with separate evolution and evaluation seeds. Physical results report 30 trials per condition per task. the research desk did not independently reproduce them; public code/data availability was not established.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper reports Harness VLA as the strongest RoboCasa365 Composite-Unseen baseline (40.1%) and LIBERO-Pro baseline (72.1%). For physical tasks it compares the same SmolVLA backbone alone with SmolVLA under EmbodiedRSI's harness.

brief.title: EmbodiedRSI reports hypothesis-guided harness evolution with transfer to five real-robot tasks
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported gains hold in broader independent trials, choosing informative physical experiments and jointly updating executable skills and code could make robot adaptation more sample-efficient without retraining the foundation model. The reported real-robot evidence is promising but narrow, and does not establish general recursive self-improvement or broad transfer.
